documentation: Keys, token, expiry and account ID from credential/get (Calling the daemon).
Feature ID CREDENTIAL_DAEMON on the signed request (FEATURES.md).
material.type access_token isn't supported: UNSUPPORTED_MATERIAL, naming the type (Calling the daemon). Non-recoverable under the Credential Refresh SEP (Credential refresh).
Session credentials with an empty access_key_id are refused (Calling the daemon).
A reply with no material.account_id succeeds, and the credentials have no account ID (Calling the daemon).
Session credentials without expires_at are refused (Calling the daemon).
Credentials that are already expired are returned as received (Calling the daemon).
expires_at with 9 fractional digits, as the credential daemon sends for aws login credentials, is accepted (Calling the daemon). expiresAt isn't given: SDKs keep the expiry at their own precision.
An expires_at that isn't an RFC 3339 timestamp is a PROTOCOL_ERROR that names the field (Calling the daemon).
A null expires_at counts as missing: PROTOCOL_ERROR (Calling the daemon).

$HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock links to a socket that nothing listens on: the not-running error names that path and how to start the daemon. terminal: SDKs whose chain moves on (Errors) assert the error from the provider.
REAUTH_REQUIRED, non-SSO profile: the error exposes the code.
REAUTH_REQUIRED, SSO profile: the error exposes the code.
configContents:
[profile dev]
sso_session = corp
sso_account_id = 111111111111
sso_role_name = ReadOnly
credential_daemon = corp
[sso-session corp]
sso_start_url = https://corp.awsapps.com/start
sso_region = us-east-1

documentation: A data.code the SDK does not know is REQUEST_REJECTED; the message carries the daemon's message and code.
CREDENTIAL_NOT_FOUND: the error exposes the code.
A -32000 error with no data.code is "the daemon rejected the request" (REQUEST_REJECTED).
A reply with both result and error is a PROTOCOL_ERROR (Calling the daemon).
A reply with neither result nor error is a PROTOCOL_ERROR (Calling the daemon).
A reply whose jsonrpc isn't "2.0" is a PROTOCOL_ERROR (Calling the daemon).
A reply line that isn't JSON is a PROTOCOL_ERROR, and the error doesn't include the line (Calling the daemon).
A reply line over 64,000 bytes is a PROTOCOL_ERROR; the SDK stops reading at the limit (Calling the daemon).
A reply line of exactly 64,000 bytes is accepted (Calling the daemon).
The daemon closes the connection without sending a line: PROTOCOL_ERROR, not NOT_RUNNING (Calling the daemon).
A reply whose id and result.credential differ from the request's is still used: SDKs don't compare them (Calling the daemon).
A profile without credential_daemon is left to the rest of the chain: the daemon isn't dialed and the next provider runs (Profile format).
credential_daemon in the shared credentials file is ignored: the daemon isn't dialed and the next provider runs (Profile format).

A name that is not a valid daemon credential name is a configuration error; the daemon is not dialed. terminal: SDKs whose chain moves on after a configuration error (Errors) assert the error from the provider.

An empty credential_daemon value is a configuration error, not an absent key; the daemon is not dialed. terminal: SDKs whose chain moves on after a configuration error (Errors) assert the error from the provider.
credential_daemon with role_arn is a configuration error. terminal: SDKs whose chain moves on after a configuration error (Errors) assert the error from the provider.

credential_daemon with web_identity_token_file is a configuration error that says the profile has two credential sources (rule 2). terminal: SDKs whose chain moves on after a configuration error (Errors) assert the error from the provider.
source_profile without role_arn on a daemon profile is ignored: the daemon is used (Profile format rule 1).
configContents:
[profile dev]
credential_daemon = dev
source_profile = other
[profile other]
aws_access_key_id = AKIDOTHER
aws_secret_access_key = s

documentation: credential_source without role_arn is ignored: the daemon is used (Profile format rule 1).
The daemon wins over static keys in the same profile.
configContents:
[profile dev]
credential_daemon = dev
aws_access_key_id = AKIDSTATIC
aws_secret_access_key = s

documentation: The daemon wins over credential_process in the same profile, and the process never runs (rule 1).
A daemon failure with static keys in the profile: the static keys MUST NOT be used (Profile format rule 1). terminal: SDKs whose chain moves on (Errors) assert only that AKIDSTATIC is not returned.
configContents:
[profile dev]
credential_daemon = dev
aws_access_key_id = AKIDSTATIC
aws_secret_access_key = s

documentation: An SSO profile sends account_id and role_name; the name is the sso-session daemon credential.
configContents:
[profile dev]
sso_session = corp
sso_account_id = 111111111111
sso_role_name = ReadOnly
credential_daemon = corp
[sso-session corp]
sso_start_url = https://corp.awsapps.com/start
sso_region = us-east-1

documentation: SSO profile with neither key: the SDK's own SSO outcome, before any daemon call (Profile format rule 3). botocore: no credentials, the next provider runs.
configContents:
[profile dev]
sso_session = corp
credential_daemon = corp
[sso-session corp]
sso_start_url = https://corp.awsapps.com/start
sso_region = us-east-1

documentation: SSO profile with neither key that also has role_arn: rule 2 doesn't apply, no daemon call, and the profile resolves as if credential_daemon weren't set (Profile format rule 3). botocore: the role is assumed with the source profile's keys.
configContents:
[profile dev]
sso_session = corp
credential_daemon = corp
role_arn = arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Admin
source_profile = base
[profile base]
aws_access_key_id = AKIDBASE
aws_secret_access_key = s
[sso-session corp]
sso_start_url = https://corp.awsapps.com/start
sso_region = us-east-1

documentation: SSO profile with only sso_account_id: the SDK's own SSO outcome (Profile format rule 3). botocore: its existing config error naming sso_role_name.
configContents:
[profile dev]
sso_session = corp
sso_account_id = 111111111111
credential_daemon = corp
[sso-session corp]
sso_start_url = https://corp.awsapps.com/start
sso_region = us-east-1

documentation: A role profile with source_profile = dev gets dev from the daemon, then calls AssumeRole (stubbed).
configContents:
[profile dev]
credential_daemon = dev
[profile admin]
role_arn = arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Admin
source_profile = dev

documentation: Linux: AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET is dialed even when $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock exists.
AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET names a path with no socket: not running, no fallback to $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock.
AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET names a regular file: the connect fails, so not running, with no fallback to $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock.
AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET is a relative path: it counts as unset, so the socket at that path isn't dialed and $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock is (Socket location).
AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET is the empty string: it counts as unset, so $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock is dialed (Socket location).
JVM SDKs: the aws.credentialDaemonSocket system property is dialed even when AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET is set and $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock exists (Socket location).
JVM SDKs: the aws.credentialDaemonSocket system property names a path with no socket: not running, with no fallback to AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET or $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock.
JVM SDKs: with the aws.credentialDaemonSocket system property unset, AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET is dialed (Socket location).
JVM SDKs: the aws.credentialDaemonSocket system property is the empty string: it counts as unset, so AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET is dialed (Socket location).
JVM SDKs: the aws.credentialDaemonSocket system property is a relative path: it counts as unset, so the socket at that path isn't dialed and AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET is (Socket location).

Nothing at $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock and no AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET: no location applies, so nothing is dialed, and the not-running error says to install the daemon or link its socket there, or to set AWS_CREDENTIAL_DAEMON_SOCKET (Socket location).
HOME unset: location 4 isn't absolute, so it is skipped even though a link is at .aws/credential-daemon.sock under the current directory; no location applies, so nothing is dialed (Socket location).
macOS with a relative HOME: location 4 isn't absolute, so it is skipped even though a link is there under the current directory; no location applies, so nothing is dialed (Socket location).
$HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock links to a missing path: not running, the error names the link and its target, and no other location is tried (Socket location).
A socket, not a link, at $HOME/.aws/credential-daemon.sock: it is dialed (Socket location).

Environment credentials win over a daemon profile picked by AWS_PROFILE in SDKs whose chain checks them first. The outcome follows each SDK's existing order for environment keys and a named profile; botocore's is given.

The web identity environment variables are set and AWS_PROFILE names a daemon profile (Specification). SDKs that check the profile before those variables use the daemon; SDKs that follow the chain precedence SEP check environment web identity first and fail on the missing token file, unless their chain moves on after that error. The token file doesn't exist, so no SDK reaches STS. botocore's outcome is given.
After a service rejects daemon credentials, the next refresh calls the daemon instead of returning the cached copy, and returns the new credentials (Credential refresh).

After a service rejects daemon credentials, the next refresh calls the daemon, which returns the same access key ID again. The refresh fails as a recoverable refresh failure with no daemon error code (Credential refresh).
